subject.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier

question: Should `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` be accepted as a core config surface, and should existing no-override subagent/cron sessions keep hook-loaded allowlist matches or become root-only by default?
rationale: The implementation is bounded, but this choice affects existing hook users, session context, prompt size, and future bootstrap-selection API shape.

options.title: Preserve no-override compatibility
options.body: Keep current no-config hook-extra behavior and apply the root-only hook guard only when users explicitly set `bootstrapTier`, then document the new setting.

options.title: Accept root-only legacy default
options.body: Merge the default behavior change only with explicit maintainer approval, public docs, and upgrade notes telling hook users to opt into `full`.

options.title: Fold into broader bootstrap design
options.body: Pause this PR and resolve tiering together with broader deterministic bootstrap/context-selection work.

recommendation.title: Preserve no-override compatibility
recommendation.body: Keep current no-config hook-extra behavior and apply the root-only hook guard only when users explicitly set `bootstrapTier`, then document the new setting.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest feature-history signal on subagent bootstrap limiting and prior review context for this exact issue.
